one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled catalyst falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29. Q4 FY26 results (Aug 25), the 10-K (Sep 9) and Investor Day (Sep 17, which reaffirmed the FY27 guide; stock -4.2%) are all past. Q1 FY27 results (guide: revenue $4.29-4.31B, non-GAAP EPS $2.44-2.48 incl. SBC) come in late November or around Dec 1, outside the window either way (the supervisor confirmed this). The Oct 16 dividend ($1.38) is immaterial. What remains is AI-agent tax and bookkeeping headline risk and software-sector flows. Momentum is negative (about $292 on Sep 23 to $268, near the $252.84 low), but at about 11.6x SBC-loaded FY27 EPS with buybacks running, a reversal bounce is just as plausible. So I stay near neutral: median about $267, log sd about 14.5% (50% annual vol / 3.5), with slightly fat tails.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E on FY28E SBC-inclusive EPS ($25.6 x 13.5x = $346, 50%) and owner-FCF yield on normalized FY28E FCF (about $24.8/share at 8% = $310, 50%), giving about $328 twelve months out.

Trimmed for TurboTax price and share pressure. Round 1 was $25.8 on 2% accretion; faster buybacks are offset by the share-loss evidence.

The stock is at 11.6x FY27 loaded EPS. Mid-teens EPS growth and heavy buybacks would support about 18x for a market-like franchise. The discount reflects TurboTax losing about 3.7 points of relative share in one season (units -2% vs IRS self-prepared e-file +1.7%), price being the top churn reason, and the ex-growth tax comp H&R Block at about 6.6x. 13.5x (from 14x in round 1) is a partial re-rating only.

bear.story: AI-native filers and price cuts keep taking TurboTax share in the 2027 season (units fall again, a deeper ARPC cut), Consumer misses its 4-6% guide, and QBO customer growth stalls. FY28 EPS is flat at about $23, and the multiple compresses to about 8x, toward H&R Block's about 6.6x, as the market treats Intuit as ex-growth. Buybacks cushion but don't prevent the de-rating.

base.story: The FY27 guide is roughly met (revenue +9-10%, EPS about $23), with TurboTax units about flat to slightly down but Live and assisted still growing. Buybacks retire about 3.5% of shares a year, and the multiple edges up to about 12x FY28 EPS of about $25.5.

bull.story: The AI-native TurboTax season halts share loss, Big Bets (assisted tax, money, mid-market IES) keep growing about 30%, and the narrative flips to Intuit as a data and distribution winner. The multiple re-rates to about 16x FY28 EPS of about $26, near the sell-side median target (about $405).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $185 the stock would trade at about 8x FY27 SBC-loaded EPS and about an 11.5% normalized owner-FCF yield ($5.3B / $49B cap). Even an ex-growth tax multiple like H&R Block's 6.6x only fits if the market expects earnings to shrink, most likely from accelerating TurboTax unit or ARPC losses in the 2027 season or QBO subscriber counts turning negative. At that point the franchise-durability thesis (Business 10-15% CAGR, Consumer 4-8%) is broken, not just de-rated. I lowered it from $190 because the true ex-growth comp multiple is lower than I assumed.

Whether the momentum-driven de-rating keeps going regardless of fundamentals (stock -62% over 1 year, near its lows)
reasoning: Primary documents show a business still growing, with growth slowing. FY26 revenue was $21.4B (+14%). The FY27 guide is revenue +9-10% (TurboTax +2-3%) and non-GAAP EPS $22.88-23.12, now fully SBC-burdened. The 10-K shows online paying customers +3% and TurboTax units -2%. Round 2 corrects my cash base: the 10-K cash flow statement and tax note (which I re-read myself) confirm the supervisor's finding. FY26 OCF of $8.84B includes a one-off +$1,279M deferred-tax add-back from the OBBBA R&D election, and cash taxes paid were only $281M vs $1,408M. Normalized owner FCF is therefore about $5.3B, not $6.6B, which cuts my FCF leg from $331 to $310. I also accept that buybacks at $268 retire about 4% of shares net (I use 3.5%, because normalized FCF less dividends cannot fully fund $5B+/yr without debt). That lifts EPS accretion, but I offset it with the share-loss datum (TurboTax about 3.7 points behind the category) and trim the multiple to 13.5x. FY28 EPS is $25.6, so the P/E leg is $346. The blended fair value is about $328 (from $345). Following the supervisor's HRB check (about 6.6x forward), my bear moves from $200 to $185 (flat EPS at about 8x) and the thesis break from $190 to $185. I keep the bear weight at 33%, not higher: HRB is a no-growth, low-buyback-yield comp, and INTU still guides +9-10% revenue. Scenarios are bear $185 (33%), base $305 (45%) and bull $420 (22%), each a lognormal with 19-24% dispersion, for a mean of about $291, a median of about $288 and P(>=$268) of about 0.575. The decisive evidence (the 2027 tax season) arrives Jan-May 2027, so I don't assume convergence to fair value. The sell-side median target (about $405) is a lagging reference only.
